Compare fitted models on the same data

Source: R/compare-models.R
compare_models.Rd

One row per model with its log likelihood, number of parameters, information criteria, classification quality and convergence, so alternative specifications (for example trajectory classes alone against a growth mixture model) are compared without assembling tables by hand. delta_bic is each model's BIC above the smallest, and bic_weight the Schwarz weight, exp(-delta/2) normalized over the models compared (Wagenmakers and Farrell 2004): the approximate posterior probability of each model if one of them is true, with equal prior probabilities.

Usage

compare_models(..., n_profiles = NULL, n_group_classes = NULL, cutoff = 0.8)

Arguments

...

Either an enumeration grid from enumerate_classes() followed by the candidates to compare (none for all of them, or a selection through n_profiles and n_group_classes); or two or more fits from multilpa(), lpa(), lca(), lta() or get_candidate(); or two or more fits from mixture_regression() (with or without random). Name fits to label the rows; unnamed fits are labelled by their expression, candidates by their name.

n_profiles, n_group_classes

With a grid, the class counts of the candidates to compare, instead of naming them; NULL takes every count. Candidates whose fit failed are left out, with a message.

cutoff

For profile and class models, the average posterior probability below which a class is counted in avepp_below and group_avepp_below. Not used for mixture regressions.

Value

A base data.frame of class latents_comparison with one row per model. For mixture regressions: model, n_classes, random, n_parameters, log_likelihood, aic, bic, sabic, icl, entropy, smallest_share, delta_bic, bic_weight, converged. For profile and class models: model, n_profiles, n_group_classes, structure (the covariance structure, NA without continuous indicators), n_parameters, log_likelihood, every information criterion of enumerate_classes()'s candidates table, profile_entropy, group_entropy, avepp_min, avepp_max, avepp_mean, avepp_below and the same four prefixed group_, smallest_share (the smallest estimated profile share, relative to all observation mass including any noise component), converged, n_best_replicated, and delta_bic and bic_weight on bic_groups (the BIC that counts groups as the independent units; on a single-level model it is the ordinary BIC). The numbers are the ones the grid's candidates table reports. No row is marked as best: delta_bic and bic_weight carry the evidence. Raises latents_bad_argument for fits it cannot compare, for a group-class family grid (compare those in their own table), for candidates named together with n_profiles or n_group_classes, and for n_profiles or n_group_classes without a grid; latents_unknown_candidate for a name or counts not in the grid; latents_failed_candidate for a named candidate that could not be fitted; and latents_incomparable_models for fits to different data. A cutoff outside (0, 1] fails the argument checks.

Details

Information criteria are comparable only on the same data: every model must be fitted to the same outcome, persons (or groups) and observations, or the comparison is refused.

Candidates of an enumeration grid are compared by naming them, as the grid's candidate column shows them: compare_models(grid, "classes3_groups4", "classes3_groups5"), or by their class counts, compare_models(grid, c(3, 4), c(3, 5)) (one number is one group class). n_profiles and n_group_classes select candidates instead: compare_models(grid, n_profiles = 3) compares every candidate with 3 profiles; compare_models(grid) compares them all. Latent class models are compared the same way; their n_profiles column counts classes. Fits from multilpa(), lpa(), lca(), lta() or get_candidate() can also be passed directly.

References

Wagenmakers, E.-J., & Farrell, S. (2004). AIC model selection using Akaike weights. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 11, 192–196.

Examples

# Fixed trajectories against growth curves with a random intercept,
# for the first 60 students
few_students <- subset(growth_scores, student <= 60)
trajectories <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, few_students, n_classes = 2,
                                   id = "student", class_level = "group",
                                   seed = 1)
growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, few_students, n_classes = 2,
                             id = "student", class_level = "group",
                             random = "intercept", seed = 1)
compare_models(trajectories = trajectories, growth = growth)
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model         Classes  Random     k    LogLik      BIC    ΔBIC  Weight  Entropy
#> ------------  -------  ---------  -  --------  -------  ------  ------  -------
#> trajectories        2  none       7  -1277.94  2584.53  196.11   0.000     0.94
#> growth              2  intercept  9  -1175.79  2388.43    0.00   1.000     0.97

# Candidates of an enumeration grid, by name, by class counts, or selected
grid <- enumerate_classes(subset(course_engagement, student <= 40),
                          c("browse", "lectures"), "student",
                          n_profiles = 2:3, n_group_classes = 1:2,
                          model = "VVI", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
compare_models(grid, "profiles2_groups2", "profiles3_groups2")
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1458.86  2958.29   0.00   0.999  3233.59     0.67       0.90      0           0.96             0.98
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1454.49  2971.70  13.41   0.001  3409.04     0.67       0.72      1           0.96             0.97
compare_models(grid, c(2, 2), c(3, 2))
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1458.86  2958.29   0.00   0.999  3233.59     0.67       0.90      0           0.96             0.98
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1454.49  2971.70  13.41   0.001  3409.04     0.67       0.72      1           0.96             0.97
compare_models(grid, n_group_classes = 2)
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1458.86  2958.29   0.00   0.999  3233.59     0.67       0.90      0           0.96             0.98
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1454.49  2971.70  13.41   0.001  3409.04     0.67       0.72      1           0.96             0.97
